title.narrative: Let Them Grow Healthy (Akule ndi Thanzi)

description.narrative: (Malawi): USAID's Let Them Grow Healthy activity will work with private sector partners and serve as the primary community-based platform for the delivery of a wide range of water, sanitation, and hygiene; nutrition, and maternal and child health interventions. With FY22 funds, the activity will finance community-level efforts to consult with mothers and caregivers on care and feeding practices for infants and young children. Using the Care Group Model, the activity will: 1) conduct nutrition education to improve knowledge and practices; 2) strengthen community referral and support systems for pregnant women and children under-5; 3) promote adequate women's nutrition, exclusive breastfeeding, and complementary feeding through social behavior change; 4) construct boreholes and rehabilitate non-functional ones; 5) facilitate the creation of open defecation-free communities; 6) promote access and adoption of improved water and sanitation services, and hygiene practices. .The activity also promotes complementary interventions such as soy processing, fruit-tree propagation, and cultivation of orange-fleshed sweet potatoes. This approach will bolster community members' confidence, capacity, and skills to act as agents of their own development process. The activity will improve the health and nutrition status of under-5 children in targeted districts. These interventions will improve nutrition and overall health outcomes among vulnerable children and women by providing cleaner and reliable water supply, diet diversity, and associated social and behavior change programming..The activity supports the Integrated Country Strategy Mission 3.1-Malawi improves individual and community agency to an extent that its citizens become more productive, engaged, and resilient, and 3.2-Malawi improves access to and quality of health services so that more of its citizens gain and retain full health and can contribute productively at home, in the community, and at work.....
